messages:
Marta: Quick question — proposing we adjust how we compute the GPU fleet SLI. Right now it’s pure 95th latency per route which hides queuing when pools hit saturation in eu-west1. Thinking to create a composite SLI: latency + queue_pressure.

Sam: Agree, latency alone underreports user impact when requests sit in scheduler queues. Do you have an example PromQL we can start from?

Marta: Sketch: we keep existing p95 for inference (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) but fold in a saturation SLI using queued requests / available GPUs. Something like: queued_ratio = sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting_total{app="inference",region="eu-west1"}) / sum(gpu_available_count{region="eu-west1"})

Ava (oncall): FWIW we saw a 3x error budget burn yesterday between 14:05-15:30 in eu-west1. Root cause was delayed node provisioning + pod churn during a model rollout. If we don't surface saturation, teams only see latency after it’s too late.

Sam: Here's a compact PromQL for saturation SLI candidate (we can iterate):
```
# queued ratio per region (5m window)
queued_ratio = sum(rate(inference_queue_length_total{job="scheduler"}[5m])) by (region) /
sum(gpu_allocatable_count{job="kube-state-metrics"}) by (region)

# latency p95 per region
lat_p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
```

Rita: For SLO targets I propose: availability 99.95% (standard), latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for production routes, and saturation SLI: queued_ratio < 0.05. If queued_ratio > 0.1 for >10m that should count as an error for the composite SLO. Thoughts?

Tom: +1 on composite, but watch blast radius. Need to ensure per-pool/node SLI not just region — eu-west1 has heterogeneous pools. Suggest tagging by pool: pool=dedicated, pool=burst.

Marta: Good point — we'll add pool label. Also want error budget reporting to be per-customer-tier and per-region. Dedicated customers should see separate burn.

Sam: Example burn-rate calc (high level, dashboardable):
```
# errors = sum of SLI violations, requests = total successful+failed requests
errors = sum(increase(inference_sli_violations_total{region="eu-west1",pool!=""}[1h]))
requests = sum(increase(inference_requests_total{region="eu-west1",pool!=""}[1h]))
# allowed errors per SLO (for 99.95 over window): allowed = (1 - 0.9995) * requests
burn_rate = errors / allowed
```
We can show cumulative burn (sum over 30d) and 1h/6h burn rates for alerting.

alertmanager-bot: Alert triggered: error_budget_burn_rate > 4 for 1h (eu-west1, pool=burst) — firing 1825902712.

Ava (oncall): We should tune alert thresholds: page on burn_rate > 8 sustained 1h, but warn when > 2 for 30m. Paging too early floods oncall, but warning needs to be visible in runbook.

Rita: Agreed. Also add an automated report to SRE Slack daily at 08:00 with per-region error budget remaining and top contributors (latency / saturation / infra errors).

Sam: I'll prototype a Grafana dashboard with panels: p95 by region/pool, queued_ratio heatmap, per-region burn_rate (1h/6h/30d), cumulative errors table, and a synthetic probe success rate. Will add annotation when autoscaler events happen.

Marta: Also add a small synthetic test that pings a lightweight model via an isolated pool and measure cold-start latency. That helps separate provisioning regressions from model perf.

Tom: For alerts PR please include: updated PromQL, alert severities (warning/page), runbook links, and a Grafana link. I can review.

Sam: Will open PR to infra/alerts and dashboards, assign to @Marta and @Tom. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

Marta: Thanks — please cc @Ava for oncall handoff.

Ava (oncall): Thanks, I'll review runbooks and add a section for regional capacity failure modes.

Rita: Nice — once live we can run a 72h smoke on the error budget reporting and adjust thresholds based on noise. :thumbsup:

Sam: Closing loop — PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/412 (will link dashboards after review).

Marta: Perfect, closing thread.
